text:
A: Hiya! Oh, it's you, with the dog! I loved your photo. Is she there now?
B: Hiya. Erm, yeah, she's just... she's under the throw, you can probably see her nose.
A: Oh my God, I can, bless her! What's her name?
B: Mabel. She's a whippet. She's a bit anxious, she's scared of the bin lorry.
A: Aw. Mine's Biscuit, the fat grey one, he's somewhere knocking things off the windowsill. I'm Lauren, by the way, sorry, I just went straight in.
B: That's alright. I'm Bethany. I saw your cat as well, in the photo.
A: Did you? He gets everywhere. So where are you, duck?
B: Pontefract. In Yorkshire.
A: Oh, not that far then, I'm Derby. My last call was with a lad from Plymouth, I didn't even know where to start with that. He was nice, though, bit cheeky.
B: Mine was a man from Castleford. That's like next door to me. He knew the flower shop I used to work at.
A: No way! Small world. So you're a florist?
B: I was. The shop closed, eighteen month ago. So I'm not really doing anything at the minute. Just... looking. Sorry.
A: Don't say sorry! Honestly, I'm the same, I was a fitness instructor at the leisure centre and they handed it to some new company and cut the timetable and that was me, gone. Five months now. I'm signing on and everything.
B: Oh no. That's horrible.
A: It is, it's proper rubbish. I tell people and I sort of laugh it off, but, you know. You feel a bit daft, don't you? Like everyone else has got somewhere to be.
B: Yeah. That's exactly it. My husband does long shifts and I'm just at home with the dog, and I feel a bit, erm, useless sometimes.
A: You're not useless! You do flowers, that's a skill. I couldn't arrange a bunch of daffs to save my life.
B: I do still do bits. Weddings for friends. And I press flowers, I make little framed ones. Them on the shelf behind me.
A: Oh, are they yours? They look lovely, I thought you'd bought them. You should be selling them! Like at craft fairs, or online.
B: I've thought about it. Doing wedding flowers from home and that. But I'm rubbish with the paperwork side. And websites. I don't know, it's just... a lot.
A: Oh, same, same! I want to do my own dance classes, for women and older ladies, in church halls and that, and I keep saying I'll do a start-up course at the job centre. Have I booked it? Have I heck.
B: Ha. I've got a wedding planning course I never finished.
A: We're as bad as each other! We should do it together, like, kick each other up the bum.
B: Maybe. That'd be nice, actually.
A: Sorry, I'm going off on one. What are you having for your tea?
B: Erm, just sausage and mash, I think. Craig's on nights so it's just me.
A: Same here, Ryan's on shifts, so it'll be a cheese cob for me. Again. Living the dream, duck.
B: Ha. I made a banana bread yesterday, it sank in the middle, so I might just have that.
A: Sunk ones taste better, everyone knows that, it's all the gooey—
